p.src: It separates central-bank liquidity (H.4.1), commercial-bank transmission (H.8), financial-conditions pressure (NFCI), external funding pressure (TIC), fiscal-flow cushioning (MTS), labor-cost pressure (ECI), and ex-post cycle dating (NBER chronology).

u.src: It separates central-bank liquidity (H.4.1), commercial-bank transmission (H.8), financial-conditions pressure (NFCI), external funding pressure (TIC), fiscal-flow cushioning (MTS), labor-cost pressure (ECI), and ex-post cycle dating (NBER chronology).
en: It separates central-bank liquidity (H.4.1), commercial-bank transmission (H.8), financial-conditions pressure (NFCI), external funding pressure (TIC), fiscal-flow cushioning (MTS), labor-cost pressure (ECI), and ex-post cycle dating (NBER chronology).

p.src: 1) Label regime state with NBER chronology for historical calibration.

u.src: 1) Label regime state with NBER chronology for historical calibration.
en: 1) Label regime state with NBER chronology for historical calibration.

p.src: 2) Compare H.4.1 versus H.8 first to test liquidity-versus-transmission divergence.

u.src: 2) Compare H.4.1 versus H.8 first to test liquidity-versus-transmission divergence.
en: 2) Compare H.4.1 versus H.8 first to test liquidity-versus-transmission divergence.

p.src: 3) Cross-check with NFCI and TIC before assuming valuation support is durable.

u.src: 3) Cross-check with NFCI and TIC before assuming valuation support is durable.
en: 3) Cross-check with NFCI and TIC before assuming valuation support is durable.

p.src: 4) Use MTS and ECI as cash-flow and cost-pressure context, then confirm with DSR/FOR and NY Fed household-stress data before increasing leverage.
